title: Lending
summary: End-to-end generic Lending business journey covering Retail/Consumer, Personal, Mortgage/Home, Auto/Vehicle, Secured/Unsecured, Installment, SME/Business, Overdraft/Credit Line, Refinancing and Top-up across application, underwriting, collateral, approval, contracting, disbursement, servicing, repayment, collections, restructuring, settlement and closure.

payload.title: Onboarding/KYC dependency
payload.content: Lending consumes authoritative customer identity, customer master, KYC/CDD, AML/screening, document and consent outcomes. It does not duplicate the complete Customer Onboarding Journey.

payload.title: Payments dependency
payload.content: Lending reuses governed disbursement, repayment, posting, reversal, settlement, reconciliation, notification and uncertain-outcome concepts while remaining authoritative for credit, facility, schedule, balance and closure.

Establish customer and channel context, select an eligible Lending family, capture borrower intent and submit a complete, consented application without imposing product-specific requirements prematurely.

payload.title: Lending – End-to-End Milestone Business Process Flow
payload.description: High-level generic Lending lifecycle from product selection and application through eligibility, underwriting, conditional collateral, approval, offer, contract, facility setup, disbursement, servicing, repayment, delinquency, restructuring, settlement and closure.

scope.start: A customer or authorized representative expresses intent to obtain or change an eligible lending product.
scope.successEnd: The approved loan or facility is activated, serviced and ultimately settled or closed through controlled, auditable outcomes.
scope.policyQualification: Exact rates, fees, ratios, thresholds, approval authority, legal requirements and timeframes follow applicable product configuration, credit policy and jurisdiction.

businessRules.rule: Only products available for the customer, segment, channel, jurisdiction and relationship context may be presented or selected.
Product-family rules must distinguish installment, revolving, secured and unsecured treatment according to applicable product configuration.
The applicant and every required borrower, co-borrower, guarantor or authorized legal-entity representative must have a valid role and relationship.
A co-borrower or guarantor is required only when the selected product or assessed credit structure requires that party.
Requested amount, currency and tenor must be captured and evaluated against applicable product and credit policy without hardcoded values in Journey content.
An application cannot be submitted until mandatory data, consent and applicable documents are complete or explicitly routed for controlled rework.
Customer identity, KYC/CDD and relevant screening outcomes must be valid or routed to their owning control process before lending approval.
Credit-bureau access requires applicable consent and a traceable inquiry purpose.
Duplicate or materially overlapping applications must be detected and resolved before a new lending decision proceeds.
Income, employment or business financial information must be verified to the level required by product, segment and applicable credit policy.
Affordability and existing-obligation assessment must use authoritative inputs and the current applicable credit policy.
Automated decisions must retain the evaluated inputs, rule outcomes, decision version and reason evidence.
Cases outside automated-decision authority or with exceptions must route to an authorized manual underwriting path.
Credit recommendations must distinguish verified fact, calculated assessment, policy result and analyst judgment.
Collateral assessment applies only when the selected lending structure requires security.
Unsecured applications must record NO_COLLATERAL_REQUIRED or NOT_APPLICABLE and continue without artificial collateral work.
Collateral ownership, valuation, legal acceptability and security documentation must be resolved before secured lending can satisfy applicable conditions.
A guarantee is effective only when guarantor eligibility, authority, consent and required documentation are validated.
Security perfection and registration requirements follow applicable policy and jurisdiction; this Journey does not prescribe registry-specific rules.
Approval must be performed only by the resolved authority for the exposure, product, segment, risk and exception context.
An author or maker must not self-approve where segregation of duties is required.
Conditional approval must identify every unmet condition, owner, evidence requirement and validity state.
Approval validity and expiry must be evaluated before offer, contract or disbursement.
The customer offer and contract must reflect the authorized amount, tenor, pricing configuration, fees concept, repayment method and conditions.
No rate, fee or legal term may be inferred from this Journey; authoritative product configuration and executed documentation govern.
Facility and loan-account setup may begin only after an accepted offer, completed contract and satisfied setup prerequisites.
Disbursement requires satisfied conditions precedent, authorized instruction, valid destination and confirmed facility availability.
Multiple or partial drawdowns are permitted only where the approved facility and product configuration support them.
A duplicate or uncertain disbursement must be reconciled before any retry.
An active loan or facility must expose authoritative balance, schedule, status and servicing information.
Repayment allocation follows the applicable product configuration and accounting rules; no universal hierarchy is assumed.
Failed, reversed, unmatched or uncertain repayments must preserve the original reference and route to reconciliation.
Past-due and delinquency treatment follows applicable policy and jurisdiction without hardcoded DPD buckets or timelines.
Collections and recovery actions require authorized ownership, traceable customer contact and controlled outcomes.
Foreclosure and repossession are conditional recovery routes for relevant secured products, never default lifecycle steps.
Restructuring, forbearance, refinancing and top-up require eligibility assessment and approval appropriate to the changed exposure.
Early settlement requires an authoritative quote, confirmed payment, financial reconciliation and applicable security-release actions.
Closure requires resolution of outstanding balances, pending transactions, disputes, commitments and applicable collateral obligations.
Every material decision, override, retry, financial adjustment and manual action must retain audit evidence.
Customer-visible status must be derived from authoritative application, facility and payment states without conflating those state domains.
